- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3% above peak or adjust downward by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment drops below 0.3 and price declines, model underestimates further drop; add 1–3% buffer to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3–5 day moving average of sentiment before adjusting forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts early in the window (first 5–7 days); apply 3–5% downward bias to first 5 days of forecast.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7), model often misjudges direction; use sentiment median as anchor for mid-term forecast adjustment.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “high-low” cycles, model tends to lag; add 1–2 day lag correction to forecast for price reversal.
